newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian coconut oil softens, copra stable.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian coconut oil softens, copra stable.

text.p: Indonesian coconut oil prices fell further on Friday on sustained poor consumer demand, while copra was stable, traders said.
They said coconut oil was quoted at 1,860 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, down from 1,880-1,890 rupiah/kg a week ago, while copra was stable at 850 rupiah/kg.
"Coconut oil prices continue to decline basically because demand is very low. But copra prices are staying the same in line with stable demand," said one trader.
"I believe some players are building up their copra stock in anticipation of a tightening in supply," she added.
"We believe that tight copra supply will automatically boost coconut oil prices," she said.
Traders said coconut oil prices weakened because of thin demand, especially from local refineries which seemed to be well stocked. Some attributed the fall to poor overseas sentiment.
"The local market simply follows developments in Manila, where the market is quite bearish. Information from Rotterdam also shows that stocks are high there," said another trader.
Manila traders said last Monday coconut oil prices were expected to move sideways there this week ahead of the Easter holiday.
Coconut oil stocks in Rotterdam increased to 26,705 tonnes on March 10 compared with 18,826 tonnes the previous weak.

Local traders said demand for palm olein, a substitute for coconut oil, had also been weak since the Moslem Eid al-Ftir festival in early February. Palm Olein prices have dropped steadily in the past four week.
